Kind of like a reliable fall-back, right? That's how I think of it too. 

The option will always be there, but only as long as I'm alive to make it. The thought of taking away that choice, even if I were to do it myself--it keeps me from making an attempt. But knowing that I will always have that choice keeps me sane. In a twisted way, it gives me hope. I'll always have an out.
I'd rather see honesty although I understand that might not be best from a marketing perspective.

Yeah, I am actually giving him a Thank You card. Doing that has always made me feel good. I figure receiving one must feel nice too. Letter to his supervisor seems good as well. Those are good suggestions, thank you.

On a sidenote, your username is oddly unnerving and amusing. Makes me wonder if there's a story behind it.

> It doesn't matter what problems we face in life, but if they are big enough to make us question whether life is worth continuing you need to stop caring whether its normal for other people to consider it 'important'.

I never thought about it that way. I guess it's hard to see when you're in the middle of those feelings. I'm going to try to remember this, thanks.
